entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Peter Nolasco, O. de M., was a 13th-century Catalan nobleman and founder of the Royal and Military Order of Our Lady of Mercy of the Redemption of the Captives, established with Pope Gregory IX's approval on 17 January 1235. This order aimed to ransom Christian captives from Muslim-held territories in the Mediterranean, with Nolasco leading multiple expeditions. The organization's success in rescuing and rehabilitating captives led to the expansion of Christian presence in the Iberian Peninsula and North Africa.

Nolasco's military campaigns were often marked by brutal suppression of Muslim populations, earning him a reputation as a ruthless Crusader leader. His efforts to secure Christian control over the Mediterranean helped shape the trajectory of European expansion into the region.

Despite his controversial legacy, Nolasco's work had a lasting impact on the Catholic Church's relations with Muslim states and the broader European Christian community.

The exact date of Nolasco's death is unknown, but it is believed to have occurred in 1256, marking the end of an era for the order he founded.
